enquiry: We read the supplied LED NIR kidney study and want to use the same concept to guide tumor boundary decisions during live surgery. Can we quote its findings as proof that the proposed sensor is ready for that use? We have no new in vivo data and no validation on our own setup. What assessment and next feasibility steps are appropriate?

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today in tumor boundary decisions during surgery, and which surgical decision should the real-time signal support?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the clinical decision and whether an intraoperative optical signal is the right answer at all.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision and pain unknown; the feasibility plan stays at assessment of the cited evidence until the decision is defined.

clarification_questions.question: What tissue property or marker defines the tumor boundary you need to detect, and how is the boundary currently defined?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether NIR contrast between tumor and healthy tissue can exist and what must be measured.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Target and contrast unknown; lab screening on representative tissue must first establish whether a spectral contrast exists.

clarification_questions.question: What tissue types and surface conditions are involved (for example, blood presence, moisture, fat, and tissue thickness accessible to the probe)?
clarification_questions.why: Optical properties of tissue, blood and moisture change the NIR signal and the probe geometry choice.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Tissue optics unknown; the sample form is treated as in vivo tissue with unmeasured optical properties.

clarification_questions.question: How does the surgical environment vary during use (motion, bleeding, irrigation, temperature changes), and what sterilization or single-use requirements apply to the probe?
clarification_questions.why: Determines robustness, sterilization path and whether the signal stays stable during surgery.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Variation and sterilization requirements unknown; robustness and sterilization are unverified for any sensor design.

clarification_questions.question: Where would the probe sit relative to the analyzer, and does the design need a fiber link or a probe without fibers?
clarification_questions.why: Decides the optical architecture and the fiber requirements for the surgical setup.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation and distance unknown; a fiber-coupled or integrated design remains open.

clarification_questions.question: What is the current reference method for confirming tumor boundaries, such as histopathology, and what accuracy does it provide?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the benchmark against which the NIR sensor must be compared in a feasibility study.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and its accuracy unknown; comparison design cannot be fixed until the reference is named.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time, regulatory pathway and budget are required for the intended clinical use?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether a feasibility study is realistic within the required approvals, timeline and resources.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; no performance claims or timelines can be given until they are defined.

flags_before_revision.detail: '14' not in the enquiry or the pages this claim cites: The study is an ex vivo proof of concept on 14 samples from 7 patients; it states that a practicable diagnostic model st

overstated: The claim says wavelengths "must be adapted" to each tissue and cancer type. S03 p.14 only says the working LED set "should be adapted to each case individually", so "must" is more certain than the source. Fix: Change "must be adapted" to "should be adapted" to each tissue and cancer type, citing S03 p.14 for the false-negative point.

not_supported: The cited page S01 p.8 discusses multispectral data synchronization and analysis. It does not say that combined methods should be considered only after each method is assessed alone, or that the gain is a hypothesis to test. Fix: Cite an AFS source page that actually discusses assessing each method separately before combining them, or remove the caveat.

not_supported: S02 p.6 shows silica fiber transmission ranges (UV-VIS 190-1200 nm, VIS-NIR 350-2400 nm) and IR fiber ranges. It does not say silica fibers suit Raman, so the Raman part of the claim is not shown. Fix: Limit the statement to the UV/Vis and NIR ranges shown on S02 p.6, or cite a source page that covers Raman fiber use.

not_supported: S03 p.10 says a representative set should include cancer type, grade and staging, but it does not say that other organs need new models. That point appears on S03 p.14, not the cited page. Fix: Keep the cancer type, grade and staging dependence citing S03 p.10, and cite S03 p.14 for the need to adapt the approach to other tissues.

overstated: S03 p.7 says biopsy size, tissue-type differences and probe position "may have resulted" in strong spectral variability. The claim states as fact that they caused it. Fix: Replace "caused" with "may have caused" and cite S03 p.7.

rule_hints: evidence_scope: A published application or a laboratory / in-vitro study is a reason to test a method, not proof that it works for a new customer, a process, or clinical use. [S03 p.3, p.10, p.14]
nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
